fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` runs its live tier on a weekly cron across every
dataset-bearing spec, bounded only by `REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES: "12"` per spec, and its own
comment records that no dollar ceiling exists in that lane: "Hard dollar caps live at the
provider dashboard (CI has none)."

Letting the criteria covered by this epic join that sweep would multiply its per-run call
count several-fold every week, in perpetuity, and would grow again with each criterion
added later. The cron is also the wrong instrument for these fixtures: they exist to catch a
criterion-rubric regression, and a rubric regression arrives with a commit rather than with
the passage of time.

## Approach

Execute a criterion's fixtures when that criterion's rubric changes.

The selection is a rebar operation, not a CI feature: a shared engine function
(`src/rebar/llm/evals/changed_criteria.py`) maps a changed-file set to the criterion ids
whose rubric files appear in it. It does NOT reimplement the criterion→rubric-path rule: it
REUSES the prior-art primitive
`rebar.llm.evals.fixture_selection.rubric_path(criterion_id, *, repo_root, gate_key='plan_review')`,
which already resolves a logical id through `criterion_prompt_id` and `get_prompt`'s
override-wins ordering. For every id in `criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')`
it resolves `rubric_path`, makes it repo-relative, and intersects that set with the changed
files. This mirrors the code-review precedent `code_review.registry.glob_triggered_overlays` /
`project_criterion_applies`, which likewise map a `changed_files` set to criterion ids.

**Both rubric storage conventions are covered because `rubric_path` resolves both.** A
built-in criterion's rubric is the packaged in-repo source
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<id>.md` (underscore prefix); a project override is
`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-<id>.md` (dash prefix, from `criterion_prompt_id`) and WINS over
the packaged copy. Because selection resolves each criterion through `rubric_path`, an edit to
EITHER form is detected. A changed path that has the rubric shape
(basename `plan_review_*.md` under the reviewers dir, or `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-*.md`)
but equals no effective criterion's resolved rubric path is UNMAPPED: it is named on stderr
rather than skipped silently, and selection still exits 0.

**Range → changed files** reuses the existing `git diff --name-only <ref>..HEAD` plumbing
shape already in the repo (`plan_review.drift_floor._drifted_paths`), not a second convention.

**CLI surface and the argparse contract.** The existing `criteria eval` verb takes a REQUIRED
positional `criterion_id` and returns exit 2 when it is empty/missing (`docs/exit-codes.md`).
This story makes the positional OPTIONAL and MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with a new `--changed-since
<ref>` flag: exactly one of {positional id, `--changed-since <ref>`} must be given. The bare
`criteria eval` with NEITHER still returns 2, so the documented "empty or missing id → 2"
contract is preserved for that form. `docs/exit-codes.md` is updated in the same change to
document the new mode: `criteria eval --changed-since <ref>` prints the selected criterion ids
(sorted, one per line) and exits 0; an unmappable rubric-shaped path is named on stderr and
still exits 0.

**Select-then-run, reconciled with the existing always-live single-criterion verb.** The
positional `criteria eval <id>` form is unchanged (always live, one criterion, needs the
`agents` extra + credentials). The new `--changed-since` form is SELECTION-first: it prints
the selection unconditionally, then runs each selected criterion live ONLY when the `agents`
extra + credentials are present (the workflow job's environment). With no model configured —
local use, a no-CI project, the test suite — it is selection-only and issues no model call, so
a non-rubric range exits 0 with no model call.

**Portability.** The trigger is operation-linked: a developer runs the command locally against
any git range and gets the same selection, and a no-CI project gets the same behavior from the
same command. The workflow job is a thin caller. The command shells out to nothing
POSIX-specific and takes its repo root from the existing resolution path.

**CI trigger classification and ref derivation.** The new job is added to `prompt-eval.yml`.
The `pull_request` trigger is INCLUDED (a rubric edit arrives on a PR — the case this job
exists for) passing `--changed-since ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}`; the `push`
trigger is INCLUDED for ordinary branches (passing `--changed-since ${{ github.event.before }}`)
and EXCLUDED for `main`, `feature/**` and `tickets` via the existing `branches-ignore`; the
weekly `schedule` trigger is EXCLUDED for the new job — the point of this child. No trigger is
NO_FILTER. The job is non-blocking (`continue-on-error`) and same-repo-only.

## Scope

The shared changed-rubric selection function (reusing `rubric_path`), its CLI flag with the
optional/mutually-exclusive positional, the `docs/exit-codes.md` update, and the workflow job
that calls it. The existing weekly live sweep keeps its current spec set.

## Non-goals

- Changing the weekly cron's behavior for the specs it already covers.
- Making the new job a required or blocking check; it stays non-blocking like the existing
  live tier.
- Any dollar-ceiling mechanism inside GitHub Actions.

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive: one new engine function, one new CLI flag (the positional becomes optional but the
existing `criteria eval <id>` invocation is byte-compatible), one `docs/exit-codes.md` row
update, one new workflow job. The offline tier (the only required check) and the weekly live
tier are untouched. Back-out is deleting the job, the flag, and the doc row; no persisted
state, no format change.

## Testing

A real CLI subprocess against temporary git repositories with seeded commits exercises the
selection across a rubric-touching range, a non-rubric range, and an unmappable rubric path;
the subprocess tier is required because the behavior includes argument parsing, git range
resolution and exit codes. A unit test covers the workflow's resolved spec list. The
repository's existing actionlint test node covers workflow validity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A range touching `plan_review_T8.md` and `plan_review_G6.md` selects exactly the
      criterion ids `T8` and `G6`; verified by a `pytest` subprocess test asserting the
      printed selection against a seeded temporary repository.
- [x] A range touching no rubric file selects nothing, exits `0`, and issues no model call;
      verified by the same subprocess test asserting an empty selection and `exit code` 0
      with no model configured.
- [x] A rubric path matching no registry criterion is named on stderr rather than skipped
      silently, and selection still exits `0`; verified by `pytest` asserting the warning text
      for a seeded `plan_review_bogus.md`.
- [x] `criteria eval` with NEITHER a positional id NOR `--changed-since` still exits `2`,
      preserving the documented contract; verified by `pytest` asserting exit code 2.
- [x] The prompt ids covered by this epic are absent from the weekly sweep's resolved spec
      list; verified by `pytest` asserting the intersection is empty.
- [x] The command produces a selection with no CI environment variables set; verified by a
      `pytest` subprocess test run with a cleared environment.
- [x] The workflow file passes the repository's existing actionlint check; verified by
      `pytest` over that node.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; a rubric-touching range selects only the
affected criteria; a non-rubric range selects none; `docs/exit-codes.md` documents the new
mode.

## Budget

**Hard cap $25**, covering verification runs while developing this child. Steady-state cost
afterwards is zero unless a rubric changes, at which point one criterion runs.
